meta.purpose: Scholarship and means-tested bursary planning for tracked senior schools. Verify official pages before applying because criteria and deadlines can change.
meta.provenance: Official school sources unless a record explicitly says otherwise.
meta.coverage: All independent senior schools currently tracked by Openday, with state grammar schools treated separately because they do not charge tuition fees.

music.publishedStandard: Around Grade 3 on two different orchestral instruments/voice, or a higher standard if offering only one.
music.selection: Application and reference; selected candidates audition/interview with the Director of Music in January, performing one piece on each instrument (or two contrasting pieces on one), plus sight-reading, aural and interview.
music.note: The current brochure explicitly says awards consider both ability and potential and expects substantial involvement in ensembles, orchestras, choirs or bands.

scholarships.deadlineLabel: Current brochure says indicate scholarship interest on registration; confirm the current application/reference deadline with Admissions.

bursary.deadlineLabel: Financial assistance should be declared on registration; contact the school before formally registering if support is essential.
bursary.value: Limited means-tested awards; assessed by an independent third party and reviewed annually.

music.publishedStandard: Approximately Grade 4 on the first-study instrument; a second study and/or voice is often offered but is not required.
music.selection: Two contrasting first-study pieces, optional second-study piece, sight-reading, aural tests and discussion of theory/musical interests.
music.note: Belmont awards run through Years 7–8; pupils can re-apply for Mill Hill awards at 13+.
music.planningStandard: Approximately Grade 4 is the published benchmark, but the school says exceptional promise is the overriding factor. A second study/voice is often offered but is not required.

scholarships.deadlineLabel: Published deadline for Creative and Sport applications for September 2027 entry; check whether Music follows the creative deadline on the current admissions calendar.
scholarships.awardValue: No fee remission at Belmont. The award is an enrichment/support scholarship for Years 7–8.
scholarships.bursaryCompatibility: Yes — bursaries can provide up to 100% support but are awarded to outstanding pupils who have also received a scholarship.

bursary.deadlineLabel: Contact the Foundation bursary team for the 2027–28 timeline.
bursary.value: May provide up to 100% of tuition fees. At Belmont, bursaries are awarded to outstanding pupils who have also received a scholarship.
bursary.compatibility: A scholarship is required for Belmont bursary consideration.

scholarships.awardValue: Scholarships normally include a fixed £500 discount from the first term's fees plus the cost of extra tuition where applicable.
scholarships.bursaryCompatibility: Yes — additional means-tested bursary funding may be applied for after a scholarship offer.

music.publishedStandard: No single public grade threshold found on the current scholarship page.
music.planningStandard: Treat this as a competitive merit award: strong performance, contribution and potential matter; ask Music for the current expected grade/profile before applying.
music.selection: Separate application for Music; scholarship assessment for 11+/13+ is in the week commencing 9 November 2026.

scholarships.deadlineLabel: Year 7 September 2027 and Year 9 September 2028 scholarship application deadline — now passed.

bursary.deadlineLabel: Apply alongside the scholarship route and tell Admissions early if attendance depends on bursary support.
bursary.value: Means-tested awards can include fully funded or heavily discounted places; largest awards are reserved for the lowest-income families.
bursary.compatibility: Bursaries are awarded in conjunction with a Scholarship Award.

music.publishedStandard: No single grade threshold is stated on the general scholarship page; use the scholarship form and Director of Music guidance.
music.selection: Scholarship application plus the school's admissions process; current forms are published on the scholarship page.
music.note: Ask specifically how orchestral-instrument need and potential are weighted.
music.planningStandard: No grade floor is published. Use the scholarship information event / Music department to test suitability; published policy frames awards as recognition of exceptional talent.

scholarships.awardCount: Not publicly stated by scholarship category.
scholarships.bursaryCompatibility: Yes — scholarship and bursary can be held simultaneously.

bursary.value: Awards can cover 50%–100% of fees; additional proportional help can include coach travel, lunches, educational trips and one instrument's music lessons.
bursary.compatibility: Can be held with a scholarship.

scholarships.awardValue: Scholarships are usually worth 5%–15% of tuition fees. Choral Scholarships may carry up to 25% remission.
scholarships.awardCount: School publishes 96 pupils currently on completely free places; scholarship counts by category are not stated on the current admissions pages.
scholarships.bursaryCompatibility: Yes — a pupil may hold both a scholarship and a bursary.

music.publishedStandard: 11+: normally two instruments with Grade 4 (or equivalent) on the principal instrument; exceptional single-study candidates may be considered. 13+: Grade 6 (or equivalent) on the principal instrument.
music.planningStandard: The grade is a minimum benchmark, not a guarantee. A competitive application should also show ensemble contribution, musicianship and strength on a second study where possible.
music.selection: Music assessment follows the main admissions process; current 11+ scholarship applications close 17 November 2026.

scholarships.deadlineLabel: 11+ scholarship application deadline for September 2027 entry.

bursary.deadlineLabel: 11+ registration and bursary deadline for September 2027.
bursary.value: 10%–100% fee reduction. Free Places cover tuition plus uniform/sports kit, coach travel, lunches, co-curricular activities such as music lessons, trips and public exam fees.
bursary.compatibility: Can be held alongside a scholarship.

music.publishedStandard: Contact the Head of Music for suitability; the public scholarship overview does not state a single grade threshold.
music.selection: Subject-head approval is required before scholarship registration.
music.planningStandard: No public grade threshold found; Harrow advises families to contact the Head of Music about suitability before scholarship registration.

scholarships.deadlineLabel: Scholarship dates are published in the school's 2026/27 scholarship timetable; eligibility/approval should be discussed with the relevant Head of Subject.
scholarships.awardValue: Current public overview does not state a standard fee-remission percentage for all scholarship types.
scholarships.bursaryCompatibility: Means-tested support is a separate route; confirm how it interacts with a scholarship offer.

bursary.deadlineLabel: Follow the 13+ admissions and financial-assistance timetable.
bursary.value: Means-tested bursary support is available; verify the current award scale and deadlines with Admissions.

music.publishedStandard: No grade threshold is stated on the current general scholarship page.
music.selection: Separate application; candidates meet the Head of Department and complete an assessment. Music assessment is scheduled in the January scholarship week.
music.note: Academic scholarships require no separate form; 11+/13+ candidates are considered through the entrance process.
music.planningStandard: No public grade threshold is stated; the award is for the most able candidates and includes a department assessment. Ask the Head of Music for the typical successful level before applying.

scholarships.deadlineLabel: Music, Drama, Sport, STEAM and Art applications due by 4pm
scholarships.awardValue: Scholarships normally provide about 5% tuition-fee remission.
scholarships.bursaryCompatibility: Yes — bursaries and scholarships are separate.

bursary.value: Means-tested support for local families who could not otherwise afford fees.
bursary.compatibility: Can be held alongside a scholarship.

scholarships.awardValue: Current admissions policy describes four Music Scholarships across 11+ and 16+: one up to 25%, one up to 15%, and two up to 10%, plus free tuition on two instruments/voice. Academic and other scholarship fee reductions are not all quantified on the public summary.
scholarships.awardCount: Music: four scholarships across 11+ and 16+ in the published policy; additional free-tuition awards may be made for sufficient merit.
scholarships.bursaryCompatibility: Yes — scholarships and bursaries are assessed separately and can both be awarded.

music.publishedStandard: Main study should be at least Grade 5 at 11+ and Grade 8 at 16+.
music.planningStandard: Grade 5 is the published floor at 11+. The school is looking for exceptional promise and explicitly values orchestral instruments, so breadth, musicianship and contribution matter beyond the grade.
music.selection: Audition day includes group singing, aural tests, sight-reading, interview and two performance pieces.

scholarships.deadlineLabel: 11+ registration, bursary and scholarship deadline for September 2027.

bursary.deadlineLabel: Bursary application deadline for the year before entry.
bursary.value: Up to 100% of fees; in some cases help can also extend to uniform, coaches and other participation costs.
bursary.compatibility: Can be awarded with a scholarship.

scholarships.awardValue: The current public scholarship page emphasises programme support, extension and challenge and does not publish a standard fee-remission percentage.
scholarships.bursaryCompatibility: Yes, but the Foundation states bursaries are awarded to outstanding pupils who have also received a scholarship.

music.publishedStandard: No single grade threshold found on the current senior-school scholarship page.
music.planningStandard: Use the 13+ creative-scholarship process and ask Music for the current instrument-specific benchmark; do not assume Belmont's 11+ Grade 4 benchmark applies at 13+.
music.selection: 13+ Academic/Creative assessment day 14 January 2027; scholarship application deadline 7 December 2026.

scholarships.deadlineLabel: 13+ Academic, Creative and Sport scholarship applications for September 2027.

bursary.deadlineLabel: Register interest with the bursary team for 2027–28.
bursary.value: Up to 100% of tuition fees; exceptional boarding assistance may also be available. Around 45 pupils attend Mill Hill each year with bursary support.
bursary.compatibility: Bursaries are awarded to outstanding pupils who have also received a scholarship.

scholarships.awardValue: A limited number of scholarships carry enhanced fee remission; the current public page does not state standard percentages for all awards.
scholarships.awardCount: Limited; exact number not publicly stated.
scholarships.bursaryCompatibility: Yes — applicants may apply for a bursary as well as a scholarship.

music.publishedStandard: No single public grade threshold stated.
music.planningStandard: Outstanding achievement or promise is the published basis. Ask Admissions/Music for the current successful-candidate standard and award value.

scholarships.deadlineLabel: Year 7 / Year 9 subject-specific scholarship applications for September 2027.

bursary.value: Limited means-tested fee assistance; current public page does not state a standard maximum percentage.
bursary.compatibility: Can be held alongside a scholarship.

schools.name: St Paul's School / St Paul's Prep

music.publishedStandard: At 11+, applicants are encouraged when working above Grade 5 on first study (Grade 6+ for piano) with a similar standard on a second instrument. At 13+, candidates are normally around Grade 6+ but the school stresses potential and notes instrument-specific differences.
music.selection: Performance plus musical assessments appropriate to entry point; 13+ includes quick study, aural tests, a short written paper and interview.
music.note: Scholarships are honorary with free tuition on two instruments; exhibitions provide free tuition on one.
music.planningStandard: At 11+, above Grade 5 (Grade 6+ for piano) with similar strength on a second instrument is the published guidance; at 13+, around Grade 6+ is a sensible official benchmark, but instrument, potential and musicianship matter.

scholarships.deadlineLabel: 13+ music entries normally close in mid-January; verify the cycle-specific date.
scholarships.awardValue: Music Scholarships are primarily honorary/enrichment awards with free tuition on two instruments; Exhibitions provide free tuition on one. No standard tuition-fee remission is stated on the current music route.
scholarships.awardCount: Not publicly stated on the current general page.
scholarships.bursaryCompatibility: Yes — Founder's Awards / bursary support is a separate means-tested route.

bursary.deadlineLabel: Apply through the admissions process and cycle-specific bursary timetable.
bursary.value: Founder's Awards can cover fees and a matching proportion of extras including uniform, trips, transport and music lessons/instrument loan.
bursary.compatibility: Bursary support is separate from merit awards.

scholarships.awardValue: 11+ Music: up to 10% tuition remission plus free instrumental tuition. 13+ Music Awards: 10% of day fee plus free tuition on up to two instruments. King’s Scholars pay the day fee instead of boarding fee. 16+ Music: 10% of day fee.
scholarships.awardCount: 13+: up to 8 King's Scholarships per year, up to 8 Music Awards plus 3 Music Exhibitions. 16+: up to 4 King's Scholarships and up to 4 Music Scholarships.
scholarships.bursaryCompatibility: Yes, but where a pupil has a bursary the monetary scholarship value may be absorbed within the bursary. Support can reach 100%.

music.publishedStandard: 11+: at least Grade 5 principal instrument. 13+: good Grade 7 standard usually expected. 16+: good Grade 8 standard usually expected.
music.planningStandard: Westminster publishes unusually clear benchmarks: for 13+ treat Grade 7 as the realistic starting standard, not merely an aspiration. Strong second study and sight-reading/aural competence matter.
music.selection: Instrumental auditions require contrasting pieces, sight-reading and ear tests; 13+ applicants are advised to arrange an informal audition with the Director of Music in the preceding autumn.

scholarships.deadlineLabel: 13+ Challenge / King's Scholarship application deadline in Year 8. Music applications follow separate autumn/winter dates.

bursary.deadlineLabel: Indicate bursary intent at registration; detailed timetable depends on entry point.
bursary.value: Up to 100% of day fees. Full bursaries can also cover uniform, travel, equipment, books and compulsory expeditions. School-wide bursary funding is approximately £2m annually.
bursary.compatibility: Can combine with Music/King's awards, although the scholarship's monetary value may be absorbed into the bursary.

scholarships.awardValue: Founder’s Scholarships: 25% fee remission. A 13+ Major Scholarship can provide 10%. Traditional Scholar/Exhibitioner titles and Music/Sport Awards do not automatically carry fee remission.
scholarships.awardCount: Not all award counts are published on the current overview.
scholarships.bursaryCompatibility: Yes — means-tested bursaries can combine with academic scholarships and Music/Sport awards up to a maximum of 100% support.

music.publishedStandard: 13+: successful candidates are generally at least Grade 6 (or equivalent) on first instrument; ideally two instruments, with a single-study candidate needing a very high standard.
music.planningStandard: Grade 6 is a useful benchmark, but Winchester explicitly weighs musicianship, potential and commitment; high-level ensemble/orchestral experience is viewed positively.
music.selection: 13+ audition includes performance, aural tests, sight-reading and discussion of music; Music Scholarships give free tuition on two instruments/voice, Exhibitions on one.

scholarships.deadlineLabel: 2027 Election / 13+ academic scholarship application deadline. Music has its own autumn application timetable.

bursary.deadlineLabel: Express interest during the application process; cycle-specific dates apply.
bursary.value: 5%–100% of fees and can include extras such as laptops, trips and co-curricular activities. Winchester reports more than £5m in annual bursary support.
bursary.compatibility: Can combine with scholarships/awards, generally up to 100% total support.
